## Hands-on 3 – C6HJR {#hands-on-3-c6hjr .smaller}

::: {.small}
**C6HJR**: the course panel, fixed effects for country and year, on record **t = −3.804 on 233 df**. The first cell centres the unemployment rate and prints nothing, the second fits the model.
:::

::: {.fs-80}
**In the workspace:** the chunk `fit-corrected` of `index.qmd`.
:::

```{webr}
#| setup: true
#| exercise: reproduce
europeanisation <- utils::read.csv(file.path(.data_dir, "europeanisation_cy.csv"))
```

::: {.fs-90}
```{webr}
#| exercise: reproduce
#| envir: global
europeanisation <- datawizard::data_modify(europeanisation, unemp_c = unemp - ______)
```
:::

:::: {.hint exercise="reproduce"}
::: {.callout-note collapse="false"}
## Hint – centring

To centre a variable on its grand mean, subtract the mean of the whole column:

``` r
europeanisation <- datawizard::data_modify(europeanisation, unemp_c = unemp - mean(unemp))
```

With fixed effects present this does not change the t-statistic, but the specification recorded for C6HJR includes it, so do it explicitly.
:::
::::

:::: {.solution exercise="reproduce"}
::: {.callout-tip collapse="false"}
## Solution

``` r
europeanisation <- datawizard::data_modify(europeanisation, unemp_c = unemp - mean(unemp))
```
:::
::::

::: {.fs-90}
```{webr}
#| exercise: reproduce-fe
#| envir: global
# the part after the | adds the fixed effects
m1 <- fixest::feols(mcosmo ~ unemp_c | ______, data = europeanisation, vcov = "iid")

# digits = 5 prints enough decimals to compare t with the value on record
print(parameters::model_parameters(m1), digits = 5)
```
:::

:::: {.hint exercise="reproduce-fe"}
::: {.callout-note collapse="false"}
## Hint – the fixed-effects syntax

In `fixest::feols`, the bar `|` separates the regression from the fixed effects. To add country and year fixed effects, list them after the bar separated by `+`:

``` r
fixest::feols(mcosmo ~ unemp_c | cntry + year, data = europeanisation, vcov = "iid")
```
:::
::::

:::: {.solution exercise="reproduce-fe"}
::: {.callout-tip collapse="false"}
## Fully worked solution

``` r
m1 <- fixest::feols(mcosmo ~ unemp_c | cntry + year, data = europeanisation, vcov = "iid")
# digits = 5 prints enough decimals to compare t with the value on record
print(parameters::model_parameters(m1), digits = 5)
```

You should get a coefficient of −0.00347, a standard error of 0.00091 and t(233) = −3.80372, which is the −3.804 on record to the third decimal: the recorded value reproduces from the published data and the published model. The argument `vcov = "iid"` asks for conventional standard errors, the kind that `plm` reported for the recorded value, which is why the two match to three decimals.
:::
::::

::: notes
My own analysis runs on the course panel, with fixed effects for country and year, in two steps. The first cell centres the unemployment rate on its grand mean, as I centred it in the analysis that I submitted, and prints nothing. With fixed effects in the model the centring changes neither the slope nor the t, but the recorded specification includes it. The second cell fits the model with feols, in which the bar of the formula separates the regression from the fixed effects. [fill the two gaps; run both] Minus three point eight zero four, on two hundred and thirty-three degrees of freedom, to the third decimal. The argument vcov equals iid asks for conventional standard errors, the kind that plm reported for the recorded value, which is why the two agree. In your report the chunk fit-corrected holds the same two steps.
:::

## Hands-on 3 – KQXUE {#hands-on-3-kqxue .smaller .output-8}

::: {.fs-80}
**KQXUE**: its own panel of 270 country-years, a fixed effect for each country, on record **t = −7.169 on 242 df**.\
**In the workspace:** the chunk `fit-kqxue` of `index.qmd`.
:::

```{webr}
#| autorun: false
kqxue <- utils::read.csv("data/analyst_KQXUE.csv")
datawizard::data_peek(kqxue)
```

```{webr}
#| exercise: reproduce-kqxue
#| envir: global
# country fixed effects only, as xtreg ..., fe fits them in Stata
m2 <- fixest::feols(cosmo ~ unemp | ______, data = kqxue, vcov = "iid")

# digits = 5 prints enough decimals to compare t with the value on record
print(parameters::model_parameters(m2), digits = 5)
```

:::: {.hint exercise="reproduce-kqxue"}
::: {.callout-note collapse="false"}
## Hint – one set of fixed effects

`xtreg, fe` removes the average of each country and nothing else, so the bar is followed by the country alone: `| cntry`.
:::
::::

:::: {.solution exercise="reproduce-kqxue"}
::: {.callout-tip collapse="false"}
## Fully worked solution

``` r
m2 <- fixest::feols(cosmo ~ unemp | cntry, data = kqxue, vcov = "iid")
# digits = 5 prints enough decimals to compare t with the value on record
print(parameters::model_parameters(m2), digits = 5)
```

You should get a coefficient of −0.00736, a standard error of 0.00103 and t(242) = −7.16867, the −7.169 on record. The 242 degrees of freedom are the 270 country-years less the 27 country effects and the slope. The Stata code of KQXUE appended the wave EB 62.0 twice, so the respondents of autumn 2004 count twice in the 2004 means of the fifteen older member states. The column `cosmo_once` holds the means with that wave counted once; replace `cosmo` with `cosmo_once` and run the cell again to see how little the slip moves the result.
:::
::::

::: notes
KQXUE built a panel of its own, which the course rebuilt from the Stata code that the analyst deposited, and gave each country a fixed effect and no year effects. The first cell loads that panel and lists its columns: the outcome is the cosmopolitan share averaged without the respondents who mention nothing, and the unemployment rate is a share of the whole population aged twenty to sixty-four, which is one reason why this t is not mine. The second cell has one gap, the fixed effect after the bar. [fill the gap; run both] Minus seven point one six nine, on two hundred and forty-two degrees of freedom, which are the two hundred and seventy country-years less the twenty-seven country effects and the slope. In your report the chunk fit-kqxue holds the same fit.
:::

## Hands-on 3 – 018OL {#hands-on-3-018ol .smaller .output-8}

::: {.fs-80}
**018OL**: 420 cells of country, year and wave, the outcome rescaled from 0 to 1, random intercepts for country, year and wave, on record **t = −1.206 on 396.9 df**.\
**In the workspace:** the chunk `fit-018ol` of `index.qmd`.
:::

```{webr}
#| autorun: false
o18ol <- utils::read.csv("data/analyst_018OL.csv")
o18ol <- datawizard::data_modify(o18ol, pos01 = datawizard::rescale(pos, to = c(0, 1)))
```

::: {.fs-80}
```{webr}
#| exercise: reproduce-018ol
#| envir: global
# random intercepts for country, year and wave; lmerTest adds the
# Satterthwaite degrees of freedom
m3 <- lmerTest::lmer(pos01 ~ unemp + (1 | cntry) + (1 | ______) + (1 | wave), data = o18ol)

print(parameters::model_parameters(m3, effects = "fixed", ci_method = "______"), digits = 5)
```
:::

:::: {.hint exercise="reproduce-018ol"}
::: {.callout-note collapse="false"}
## Hint – the random intercepts and the degrees of freedom

Each `(1 | x)` gives the cells that share a value of `x` an intercept of their own, so the missing one is `(1 | year)`. `parameters::model_parameters()` reports the degrees of freedom that `ci_method` names, and `lmerTest` provides the Satterthwaite approximation, `ci_method = "satterthwaite"`.
:::
::::

:::: {.solution exercise="reproduce-018ol"}
::: {.callout-tip collapse="false"}
## Fully worked solution

``` r
m3 <- lmerTest::lmer(pos01 ~ unemp + (1 | cntry) + (1 | year) + (1 | wave), data = o18ol)
print(parameters::model_parameters(m3, effects = "fixed", ci_method = "satterthwaite"), digits = 5)
```

You should get a coefficient of −0.00203, a standard error of 0.00169 and t = −1.20627 on 396.92 degrees of freedom, the −1.206 on record. The year in the file is the one that 018OL took from the names of its data files, which put the wave EB 79.3, fielded in 2013, in 2012; the column `year_fieldwork` holds the true year, and a rebuild that dates every wave by its fieldwork gives t = −1.606 instead.
:::
::::

::: notes
018OL worked on four hundred and twenty cells of country, year and wave rather than on a panel of country-years, with the five cosmopolitan items averaged for each respondent first, the outcome rescaled to run from nought to one, and random intercepts for country, year and wave in place of fixed effects. The first cell loads the file and rescales the outcome, and prints nothing; the second has two gaps, the missing intercept and the name of the approximation for the degrees of freedom. [fill the gaps; run both] Minus one point two zero six, on three hundred and ninety-six point nine Satterthwaite degrees of freedom. The two packages of the model loaded with the deck, and in your report the chunk fit-018ol fits the same model with lme4 and lmerTest. One thing to notice: the file dates the last wave a year early, and a rebuild that dates it correctly does not give the recorded value.
:::
